title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: Although the system that managed the linking of the First Flame had rung the bells to resurrect the past Lords of Cinder when needed, not all of them have awakened from their resting places. Consequently, once the Flame eventually goes out, at some point these Lords of Cinder from the past will rise again and wander the lands like tiny flames. These beings will possess fragments of the First Flame stored within their bodies in the form of cinders, giving them the powers of the Flame in a world that will be enveloped in Darkness.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
The original Lord of Cinder was Gwyn, although more would link the flame and extend the Age of Fire in subsequent eras. Becoming a Lord of Cinder entails a sacrifice, as the Lord is consumed by the First Flame in the process. After Gwyn linked the flame, only his mere husk defended it; with each subsequent linking of the Flame, remnants of each new Lord of Cinder would merge with the previous ones' and strengthen the First Flame's guardian, eventually taking the form of the Soul of Cinder.

Throughout history, countless aspiring Lords were lost attempting to reach the Flame; among those who succeeded, some ultimately lacked the strength to withstand its power, and were burned to ash by the Flame instead of linking it. These individuals came to be known as Unkindled: ill-fated champions who were buried in the Cemetery of Ash, a graveyard which scarcely saw any visitors.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, the First Flame is so weakened that Lords of Cinder past are resurrected so that the embers of the First Flame inside them serve as fuel for new Linkings. Prince Lothric, who was raised to become the next Lord of Cinder, refused to Link the First Flame, while three of the resurrected Lords of Cinder refused to be used as fuel, leading to resurrection of several Unkindled in the hopes that one of them might slay the fleeting Lords of Cinder and Lothric, and Link the First Flame.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, Prince Lothric, who was raised to become a Lord of Cinder, refused to link the First Flame. This led to Lords of Cinder from the past being exhumed from their graves: these Lords were meant to sacrifice themselves to the Flame once again, using what little embers remained within themselves as kindling. However, most of these Lords refused the call, and instead settled back into their domains. To prevent the First Flame from dying out, the Unkindled would then be resurrected as a last resort; these Champions were bound to seek the absconded Lords of Cinder, and forcefully bring them back—in the form of their cinders—to their empty thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once all five Lords "sat" their thrones, an Unkindled Champion would be bestowed the embers of these Lords, and sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to overcome the final challenge and link the Flame.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lords of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : The are characters who have linked the First Flame throughout the history of the *Dark Souls* universe.

To "link the First Flame" is to reach it, be powerful enough to withstand its power, and rekindle the flame anew; it is done in order to stop the First Flame from withering out and dying, a process that occurs naturally over time and would mean both the end of the Age of Fire and the coming of an Age of Dark. To attempt to link the flame, one must typically reach the kiln built around the First Flame and defeat the empty husk of the previous Lords of Cinders guarding it against those not worthy of its power.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lords of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : The Lords of Cinder are beings that have linked the First Flame and prolonged the Age of Fire through the centuries. Although many of these champions have followed the sacrifice of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, not everyone became a Lord of Cinder through heroic deeds or even of free will. One such case is Aldrich, who became a Lord only because he had the strength to become one, despite having obtained such power by devouring an untold number of humans for his own pleasure.

The continuous linking of the Flame eventually culminated in the Soul of Cinder, the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who linked the Flame throughout history. This being, although appearing as an empty husk, inherits the abilities of the Lords of Cinders who have come before. It has long existed as the Flame's last defense inside the Kiln, protecting it from Champions attempting to link it again and acting as the ultimate test of their strength.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
The prince's decision led the system managing the linking of the Flame to resort to an emergency measure: ringing the bells and awakening the Lords of Cinder of the past from their graves, beings who had previously linked the Flame, to unite their cinders and energize the fading Flame. However, most of the awakened Lords of Cinder refused to sacrifice themselves again and returned to their lands, leaving their thrones at the Firelink Shrine empty.

The ringing of the bells would also awaken the Unkindled, who would hunt down the Lords of Cinder and bring their cinders back to Firelink Shrine. Many of these Unkindled attempted to storm the castle to slay Lothric, but were all killed by the royal guards or by his brother Lorian.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet:
Due to a curse triggered by the four female relatives of an unknown oracle, which also turned them into careless greedy creatures, the Profaned Flame was unleashed, a flame that never goes out. Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder to put the Profaned Flame to rest, even as many spoke insincerely of his role. However, after he became a Lord of Cinder, the hellish flame fell out of the sky and destroyed the city, yet consuming naught but human flesh, incinerating the human inhabitants. The flame, despite deriving from Dark and the Abyss, actively sought to harm humanity.

Before linking the First Flame, he gave his other Storm Ruler to Siegward, who promised to end Yhorm's suffering if he ever returned to life.

title: First Flame
snippet: Desperate to ensure that their Age of Fire continued, and afraid of the coming Dark, the Lords did everything they could to keep the First Flame lit. Gwyn's clan linked the sacred bonfires that were tied to the Flame to humanity, and shepherded the humans who worshipped them to kindle the flames. The Witch of Izalith attempted to use her own powerful soul to create a new First Flame, but this attempt failed, instead creating the perverse Flame of Chaos and transforming the Witch into the Bed of Chaos, which would go on to birth the race of Demons.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: At the close of a period in the Age of Fire, The Abyss Watchers linked the First Flame, becoming Lords of Cinder. An indefinite amount of time later, the destined Lord of Cinder Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame, which led to Lords of Cinder from the past being exhumed from their graves, to once again serve as kindling for the Flame. The Abyss Watchers refused to once again sacrifice themselves to the Flame, instead returning to Farron Keep, leaving their throne at Firelink Shrine empty.

title: Ludleth of Courland
snippet: When the link of fire was threatened, the Lords of Cinder would be exhumed from their graves to once again serve as kindling for the First Flame. Ludleth was among those resurrected; though unlike the other three Lords, he accepted the call, and took up his throne at Firelink Shrine to await his fate.

title: First Flame
snippet: By the time of *Dark Souls III*, many other such sacrifices, who have become posthumously known as Lords of Cinder, have given themselves to the First Flame, and the Age of Fire has persevered for many generations as a result. However, when the latest individual chosen for the honour, Prince Lothric, abandons his duty by refusing to link the fire, a desperate attempt to save the fading Flame begins. Four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected to link the fire once more, however - aside from Ludleth of Courland - they too choose to flee their duties, forcing the Ashen One to drag them back.

snippet:
The Ashen One, fights their way through the cemetery but finds their way blocked by Iudex Gundyr, an ancient golem tasked with judging the pretender Lords of Cinder

The Ashen One is welcomed by the Fire Keeper who declares herself to be at their service, as it is the duty of the Unkindled to link the Flame, urging them to find the previous Lords of Cinder and return them to their thrones, so that they can become fuel for the Flame

title: Age of Dark
snippet: Following the failure of this first contingency plan, a second plan is activated: Unkindled, those who had previously tried to link the First Flame but who had failed to do so, are resurrected from their graves in the Cemetery of Ash, and tasked with placing the rebellious Lords of Cinder upon their thrones so that the First Flame might be linked once more. The Ashen One, protagonist of *Dark Souls III*, is one of these Unkindled. After the Ashen One defeats each of the Lords of Cinder and places their remains upon their respective thrones in the Firelink Shrine, the Fire Keeper removes the embers of the Lords and bestows them upon the Ashen One, making them a "true lord, fit to link the fire," and imbuing them with the power to proceed to the Kiln of the First Flame.

title: Soul of Cinder
snippet:
Soul of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : The Soul of Cinder is the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who have linked themselves to the First Flame through history, becoming Lords of Cinder, and thus is an entity possessing all the abilities of the previous Champions despite just being an empty husk.

It exists as the Flame's last defense inside its Kiln, protecting it from anyone attempting to link it again and acting as the ultimate test of their strength—a role that it has enacted for a very long time, confronting all who entered the Kiln as aspiring Lords.

When tested by an aspiring Champion, the Soul of Cinder would even bring out the remnants of the will and power of the first one to ever link the First Flame: Lord Gwyn himself.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - soul_of_cinder 
 soul_of_cinder : After returning to the shrine, the Ashen One places the ashes of the Lords on their thrones, and the Firekeeper channels their strength to the Ashen One. The Firekeeper bids the Ashen One travel to the First Flame. Accepting the strength of the Lords, the Ashen One is transported to a copy of the Firelink shrine, standing amid the wreckage of kingdoms. From there, the Ashen One proceeds to the Kiln of the First Flame.

There they encounter the Soul of Cinder, a manifestation of the Lords that had previously linked the flame. The Soul of Cinder takes on many forms and fighting styles, mimicking those who had linked the flame. Once the Ashen One weakens it, the Soul of Cinder assumes the style of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, first one to link the flame. After defeating the Soul of Cinder, the Ashen One is presented with four options depending on the choices they made.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: In Ending 2: "The End of Fire", the First Flame is snuffed out, albeit with the Fire Keeper revealing that one day "tiny flames will dance across the darkness", which suggests that the First Flame partially perseveres in the form of embers within the Lords of Cinder of the past. As these Lords will use these embers of the First Flame to exert influence the world, this Age of Dark does not spell finality for the Flame. Alternatively, the player can choose to intervene as the Fire Keeper is about to extinguish the First Flame, by killing her before the cinematic ends. In this ending, the Ashen One instead takes the First Flame for themselves while the final segment of the opening narration is heard: *"Nameless, accursed Undead, unfit even to be cinder...And so it is...that Ash seeketh embers."*

title: Lothric
snippet: In the beginning, the first Fire Keeper had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a barren plane of endless darkness. Acting to ward off an Age of Dark, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition of Courland, rose to the challenge of becoming a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. Despite his feeble appearance, Ludleth managed to muster the strength necessary to become a Lord, something for which he himself expresses remorse, asking to be forgiven. Ludleth was exiled from his country and collaborated with Lothric to ensure that the Fire Keeper was deprived of her eyes, as well as all future maidens, to prevent them from observing a future without the Flame. The original eyes were sealed away in an enigmatic instance of Firelink Shrine, where the First Flame had all but gone out.

Lord Gwyn bequeathed most of his power to the Gods, and burned as cinder for the First Flame, but even so, Lord Gwyn's soul is a powerful thing indeed.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: In *Dark Souls III*, countless beings have prolonged the Age of Fire, preventing its end and holding off the coming of the Age of Dark. By the time the game begins, there are countless Lords of Cinder - those who successfully linked the First Flame before - and even more Unkindled who were unsuccessful. Eventually the one anointed to next link the Flame (and indeed, who was born for that very purpose), Prince Lothric, rejected the idea that the Age of Fire should be prolonged any further and instead desired to end what he called the "fire-linking curse." A contingency plan was then activated, in which previous Lords of Cinder were resurrected in hopes that they, who had linked the First Flame before, might do so again. However, by this time, the world that had been created during the Age of Fire had become a twisted shadow of its former self. snippet: Even after possibly hundreds of thousands years after the first linking of the Flame, Frampt (or other serpents affiliated with his ideology) continued to propagate the cult of the linking of the Flame; influencing kingdoms, rulers and simple Undead to continue the tradition started by Gwyn. When the First Flame drifted up to position itself on the nascent kingdom of Lothric, Frampt or other serpents affiliated with his ideology reached the city too. Over time the serpents passed on the culture of linking the Flame to the royal family of Lothric, pushing them to preserve the tradition and actively produce heirs capable of becoming Lords of Cinder. Frampt or his kin were represented in numerous statues, on par with the Three Pillars of Lothric, with elegant clothes and angel wings, showing their central role within the kingdom, considered "divine messengers". title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Despite the message "Lord of Cinder Fallen" appearing when they die, the flaming state they have in the second phase, and Lothric having a throne dedicated to him in Firelink Shrine, the Twin Princes are thought to not have ever linked the flame. There are several points in the game that suggest this:
#The description of their soul implies that they never became Lords of Cinder.
#They are not shown in the opening cinematic, meaning they were not resurrected when the bell tolled, implying that Lothric never took his throne in the first place.
#Emma, High Priestess of Lothric Castle wishes for Lothric's soul to be saved by becoming a part of the firelinking ritual, implying again that Lothric never took his throne in the first place.
#After returning all Cinders of a Lord to their thrones, Lothric's head is the only one that still has its flesh.

Lord Gwyn, bearer of the ultimate soul, divided that power among his great clan before linking the flame. But he did keep his crown, perhaps to preserve a symbol of the monarch, for its actual power had fully subsided.

title: Dark Lord
snippet:
Dark Lord -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : **This section of the lore lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations**

The Dark Lords are beings who were meant to become Lords of Cinder, but refused to link the First Flame and extend the Age of Fire, with the specific intent of bringing forth the Age of Dark (also referred to as an "Age of Man"). Dark Lords, while powerful enough to overcome the trials involved in linking the Flame, apparently don't have to inherit a primordial force (such as the First Flame) in order to be deemed worthy of their title. For instance, if the Chosen Undead chooses to become a Dark Lord, abandoning the power of the First Flame, several primordial serpents will nevertheless bow before their new Lord (including both Kaathe and Frampt), even as the Chosen Undead lacks the extraordinary power granted by the Flame.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet: Lothric, the younger prince, was the destined Lord of Cinder, who would sacrifice himself as fuel for the First Flame to uphold the Age of Fire. The prince, born a sickly, frail child, was nevertheless viewed as the "last hope of his line", the culmination of generations of Lothric rulers obsessed with producing worthy Champions for the Flame. For the anticipated journey of the young prince to the Kiln of the First Flame, a platinum sword was crafted and blessed with strong magic by the High Priestess, long before he was ready to fulfill his destiny. Oceiros created extensive propaganda around Lothric, not only giving him the name of the kingdom, but also building statues that depicted him with his sacred sword ready to complete his task, as well as preparing his throne at the Firelink Shrine in advance.

title: Lothric
snippet: During the founding of Lothric, the First Flame drifted north towards the kingdom, forever marking the history and culture of its people. Due the presence of the Flame, the lands of the world began a geographical and temporal drift towards the city of Lothric, owing to the space-time altering effects of **Convergence.****** One or more Primordial Serpents developed an interest in propagating the cult of Firelinking within Lothric, to uphold the Age of Fire and the tradition started with Gwyn's sacrifice. Eventually Frampt or other serpents affiliated with his ideology reached the city. Over time, serpents passed on the Firelinking culture to the royal family of Lothric, pushing them to uphold the tradition and actively produce heirs capable of becoming Lords of Cinder. Primordial serpents were depicted in numerous statues, on par with the Three Pillars of Lothric, with elegant clothes and angelic wings, showing their central role within the kingdom and their perception as divine

title: Champion Gundyr
snippet: Considering that those who had deceived Gundyr had given him his halberd and charged him with linking the Flame, they must have had a position superior to the king of Lothric but still close to him. This could point to the involvement of Gwyndolin, king of the gods of Irithyll, who had strong ties to Lothric; or the Primordial Serpents, who were already advisors to the royal family. Using Gundyr as a golem to test the strength of future Champions would ensure that those overseeing the linking of the Flame would be guaranteed to find potential Lords with enough power to prolong the Age of Fire.

title: Lothric
snippet:
Lothric -  Dark Souls III - location - firelinking_duty 
 firelinking_duty : The tradition of linking the Flame plays a central role in Lothric, testified by the Firelink Shrine's location just outside the city walls, connected to the Royal Gardens. A large number of people throughout the long history of the kingdom came here to take part in the ritual initiated by Lord Gwyn's sacrifice. Those who failed, becoming the Unkindled, were buried near the Shrine in the Cemetery of Ash. Next to the Cemetery was an arena complete with stands, where Iudex Gundyr's golem judged those who aspired to become Lords, testing their strength. The ritual of the linking of the Flame permeated the kingdom at every level up to the royal family, who were obsessed with producing a worthy Champion in their line to preserve their divine mandate as the guardians of the Age of Fire.

title: Kiln of the First Flame (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Kiln of the First Flame (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : The new version of the familiar place is where lies the First Flame and its guardian, the Soul of Cinder. The location has been greatly altered since its depiction in *Dark Souls*.

Once the player has gathered all of the Lords of Cinder, the Fire Keeper will perform a ritual in which the flames of the Lords will drift to her hands. She will then scatter the flames onto the player, teleporting them to the Kiln of the First Flame.

title: Lothric
snippet: Over time, the ritual of the Linking of the Fire evolved, from a simple temple inside the Royal Gardens to an arena complete with stands, in which Iudex Gundyr's golem would judge those who aspired to become Lords. Countless people throughout the long history of the kingdom came here to take part in the ritual started with Gwyn's sacrifice. All the Fire Keepers who served their purpose of guiding their Champions would be disposed of and dropped inside the Bell Tower of Firelinking Shrine, piling in up in the dozens. Even more were those Champions who tried and failed to link the Flame, becoming the Unkindled, and were buried near the shrine in the Cemetery of Ash, a graveyard of all those who failed in their task.

title: Lothric
snippet:
The relations between the two realms soon blossomed into an alliance, formalized by the incorporation of the sword of Lothric, a symbol of that realm, into the insignia of the Blades of the Darkmoon, the predecessors of the Blue Sentinels and the Way of Blue. In practice, the unification of cultural and religious symbols of the kingdoms allowed the usage of transport demons by those bearing the banner of Lothric.

Now in possession of the knowledge provided by the primordial serpents and the ancient gods of Anor Londo, the kingdom of Lothric developed its role in the linking of the Flame, building the Firelink Shrine just outside the city walls, neighbouring the Royal Gardens, in order to guarantee safe and regulated passage to the Kiln of the First Flame. The shrine would once again accept Fire Keepers who assisted Champions that aspired to link the Flame, drawing out the strength of the souls they acquired to aid them in their journey.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Having secured absolute dominion over the world, Gwyn thus began the Age of Fire, a time of prosperity that was characterized by the power of the First Flame and the vision of the Great Lord. Gwyn's clan placed themselves atop the new world order, assuming the role of deities for humans who were their subjects, and Gwyn took the title "god of sunlight". Humans venerated the gods who lived in the city of Anor Londo in the region of Lordran, building an economy and culture around the use of souls, even hunting the descendants of dragons for sport and domesticating some of them. Gwyn left the other two Lords to tend to their own domains: Izalith built her civilization underground where she and her daughters continued to study flame sorcery, and Gravelord Nito remained in the Catacombs to oversee the dead.

title: Farron Follower
snippet: As the First Flame continued to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, the Lords of Cinder of the past were exhumed from their graves to once again be used as fuel. Among them the Abyss Watchers too rose from their graves, but refused to sacrifice themselves again to link the Fire, choosing to return to their Keep in Farron. However, the Followers were no longer present to cull the warriors that would become corrupted by the Abyss, consequently forcing the Watchers to do so themselves, wasting their strength to kill each other to contain the spreading corruption.

title: Courland
snippet: At a certain point the First Flame began to fade again and the first Fire Keeper of Lothric had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a "barren plane of endless darkness". For this reason, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition, was called to become a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. Defying his frail appearance, Ludleth managed to muster the strength necessary to become a Champion, something for which he himself expresses remorse and asks to be forgiven. Despite his role, Ludleth was then exiled from his country and collaborated with Lothric, ensuring that the first Fire Keeper was deprived of her eyes and that all future maidens like her were deprived of their sight, to prevent them from observing the future without the light of the First Flame. title: Age of Dark
snippet: The idea that the linking of the First Flame was unnatural and that it ran contrary to the order of the world is an important concept in the *Dark Souls* series, especially as the Age of Fire is prolonged perpetually by innumerable successive individuals seeking to prevent the coming of the Age of Dark.

title: Ashen One
snippet: ***The End of Fire**: If the Ashen One gave the Eyes of a Fire Keeper to the Fire Keeper, they may summon her upon defeating the Soul of Cinder. The Fire Keeper will take the First Flame into her hands. She states that the fire quickly fades and that dark will soon settle, but predicts that one day, tiny flames will dance across the darkness, like embers linked by lords past, suggesting that the other Lords of Cinder of the past will one day rise and wander through the darkness with their own fragments of the First Flame. As the absolute darkness settles upon the world, the Fire Keeper asks if the Ashen One can still hear her.

title: Ashen One
snippet: firelink_shrine_dark_souls_iii_firelink_shrine : Inside the shrine, they encounter the Fire Keeper, who tells the Ashen One that the Lords of Cinder—Aldrich, Devourer of Gods, Yhorm the Giant, the Abyss Watchers, and Lothric, Younger Prince—have abandoned their thrones, and charges them with bringing the lords back. The Fire Keeper offers to channel souls in order to increase the Ashen One's strength. Also in the shrine are Blacksmith Andre, a smith from the Age of Gods; the Shrine Handmaid, who offers an expanding store of goods in exchange for souls; Hawkwood the Deserter, a crestfallen warrior; Ludleth of Courland, the last remaining Lord of Cinder who offers the Ashen One advice and the art of soul transposition (provided the Ashen One can provide him with a Transposing Kiln); and Nestling, a bird who offers to trade items. The shrine is populated by more character as the game progresses: Ringfinger Leonhard, a servant of the goddess Rosaria, who urges the Ashen One to invade the

title: Londor
snippet: close_of_an_age_of_fire : As the First Flame faded and Prince Lothric refused to link it, the Unkindled were exhumed from their graves to hunt down the Lords of Cinder of the past that had refused to return to their "thrones" and serve as fuel for the Flame a second time. It was at this pivotal moment that Londor and the Sable Church decided to make their move. Hundreds of Hollows were exiled from Londor, sent away to Lothric on a pilgrimage with the specific goal of "dying". They were equipped with shell-shaped protections chained to their backs, similar to ones found on robes of clerics that warded off stagnant darkness during long journeys which could manifest as Pus of Man. Finally these pilgrims were taught a dark miracle, the only tale known to them, that they believed carried words of forgiveness; in reality they were cursed by this magic, which attracted more attention from foes, and presumably accelerated their "preordained death".

title: Unkindled
snippet:
Unkindled -  Dark Souls III - storyline - background 
 background : To "link the First Flame" is to reach it, be powerful enough to withstand its power, and rekindle the flame anew. The Unkindled were strong enough to overcome the challenges of reaching the Kiln of the First Flame, but lacked the strength needed to withstand the power of the Flame: the primordial Fire burned them to ash, not fueled enough to properly spark anew. These failed champions' remains were entombed in the Cemetery of Ash.

title: Lore
snippet:
Gwyn, in a final effort to save the Age of Fire, marches with a great deal of his army to the Kiln of the First Flame and sacrifices himself to link with the First Flame, turning the Kiln to ash and incinerating his entire army (making them the Black Knights, who later walk Lordran). The attempt is temporarily successful, however, as the Age of Fire was only extended for at least 1000 years. Gwyn became a Hollow and is from then on known as "Gwyn, Lord of Cinder".

The Four Kings became corrupted and were seduced by evil at some point by Kaathe after Gwyn's fall and their servants turned into Darkwraiths. In an effort to stop them New Londo was flooded with all of its population, trapping the Four Kings with their Darkwraiths in the Abyss.

Soon after, the deities began leaving Lordran. Gwyndolin was the only one of Gwyn's children to stay behind...

This event leads to the creation of Gundyr's ballad, staining the reputation of the Royal Family for all years to come

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: As the First Flame continued to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, the Lords of Cinder of the past were exhumed from their graves to once again be used as fuel. Among them was Aldrich who, like the other exhumed Lords, had no intention of sacrificing himself again, as his reflections on the state of the world had led him to understand that an Age of the Deep would soon arrive, motivating him to devour the gods themselves, in order to erode their hold on the Flame and accelerate the coming of his vision. Gathering an army of deacons from the Cathedral of the Deep led by Archdeacon McDonnell, Aldrich would march on Irithyll, intent on capturing Anor Londo to devour the king of the gods himself. However, he would find his way blocked by Sulyvahn and his knights, as the Pontiff had no intention of relinquishing the source of his control over the city and the Way of White so easily. From the ensuing battle Aldrich emerged victorious, slaughtering Sulyvahn's troops and defeating

title: Unkindled
snippet:
Unkindled -  Dark Souls III - storyline - plot 
 plot : By the times of *Dark Souls III*, Prince Lothric, the destined Lord of Cinder of his generation, has refused to link the First Flame. This led to the resurrection of four Lords of Cinder of the past, whose conjoined, withered embers could kindle the First Flame in Lothric's stead. Aldrich, Saint of the Deep; Yhorm the Giant, the Abyss Watchers, and Ludleth of Courland were expected to sacrifice themselves as kindling once again. When all Lords except Ludleth rejected this duty, the Unkindled too were resurrected as a last resort, who were fated to seek out the Lords (including Prince Lothric) and bring them back to their thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once the cinders of the Lords were restored to their thrones, an Unkindled champion would be bestowed the embers of the First Flame that remained within their cinders, and finally sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to complete their journey.

title: Farron Follower
snippet: At some point, the Abyss Watchers would become Lords of Cinder, sacrificing their shared power in the wolf blood to link the fading First Flame. With the wolf blood dried up, the Undead Legion's numbers rapidly dwindled. Over time, the land of Farron, where the bodies of countless warriors of the past were buried, fell into ruin and became a rotten and poisonous forest, and the remaining acolytes of the Undead Legion were corrupted, their descendants becoming Ghrus. The Farron Followers lost their role and reason to exist along with their home, and went hollow, surviving as a wandering pack of Hollows. They drifted aimlessly until they were eventually drawn into the Painted World of Ariandel, where they were welcomed by the other forlorn souls and found refuge.

title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Ending (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - ending 
 ending : Fulfilling the purpose for which they were brought back to life, the Ashen One links the First Flame and becomes a Lord of Cinder. The Flame connects with their body, slowly setting them ablaze as they sit beside the bonfire.

Although in theory, this leads to a continuation of the once-glorious Age of Fire, this linking of the Flame is but a shadow of the linking as can be performed by the Chosen Undead in *Dark Souls*, echoing the significant weakening of the First Flame, which instead of engulfing the Kiln into an explosive blaze of fire remains weak, barely kindled anew. The world remains dim and covered in ash, with the sun still obscured by a fire-dripping eclipse that resembles the Darksign, further exemplifying that this prolonged Age of Fire will pale when compared to days of old.

title: Humans
snippet:
Humans -  Dark Souls III - character - last_days_of_fire 
 last_days_of_fire : Many millennia—or even more—have gone by, and the linking of the Fire has become a staple in the world. Finally, when the new "Lord of Cinder" Prince Lothric was destined to sacrifice himself to the Flame, he refused and opted to watch the Age of Dark settle. To save the Age of Gods, four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected as Undead, but three of them either sought the Age of Dark, or no longer cared either way. One last contingency plan existed, to awaken the Unkindled, those who had previously failed to prolong the Age of Fire with their sacrifices. Kaathe's will has been reinterpreted by the Sable Church of Londor, who aim for a different Age of Dark than what Kaathe sought; an age ruled by a Lord of Hollows.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - description 
 description : The Aldrich Faithfuls protect Lord Aldrich from harmful ash, such as the Ashen One, and claim Human Dregs as their prizes. These may be used to rank up in the covenant for rewards.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : To join the Aldrich Faithful covenant, the player must first have cleared the area by defeating both Sulyvahn's Beasts and then proceed to Archdeacon McDonnell's remains and pray to them, at this point they may ask to join and obtain proof of the covenant.

Killing the Sulyvahn's beasts is not required to join the covenant. If one wears the Slumbering Dragoncrest Ring and casts Hidden Body just as they reach the bottom of the ladder, they can sneak around the left, far wall and avoid the beasts and pray to McDonnell, thus joining.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Aldrich Faithful** is a covenant in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - benefits 
 benefits : Like the Watchdogs of Farron, Aldrich Faithful will be called upon to defend Aldrich's territory from trespassers; any player who has Host of Embers status will be subject to invasion. This area is defined as anywhere from the courtyard upon exiting Pontiff Sulyvahn's arena, up until the rotating stairway leading up to Anor Londo. Aldrich Faithful can pursue trespassers up into the cathedral itself, but will not be summoned for trespassers who have already reached the upper level bonfire.

Defeating the Host of Embers will reward all present Aldrich Faithful with Human Dregs, which can be offered to Archdeacon McDonnell to deepen their allegiance to the covenant.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - location 
 location : The Aldrich Faithful covenant can be found in the lower plane of Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.

From the Pontiff Sulyvahn bonfire, proceed onward and make way to the other side of the large courtyard with several dead Giant Slaves. Upon entering the main building on the opposite side, hit the wall on the left to reveal an illusory wall concealing the main access to the covenant.

Climb down the large ladder to reach a big, flooded hall. There are two Sulyvahn's Beasts lying in wait once reaching this area, one on the left and one further ahead on the right.

In one corner of the room lie the remains of Archdeacon McDonnell. Interacting with him allows access into the covenant.
